question: What safety and accessibility priority does the MUTCD establish for temporary traffic control planning and operation?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD establishes that the safety and accessibility of both road users and workers should be an integral, high-priority element of every project involving temporary traffic control (TTC), from planning through design and construction. This priority extends to all motorists, bicyclists, pedestrians (including those with disabilities), and workers, and is reflected in the seven fundamental principles of TTC. Note that these provisions are Guidance (recommended), not mandatory Standards. Guidance (recommended): - "Road user and worker safety and accessibility in TTC zones should be an integral and high-priority element of every project from planning through design and construction." Maintenance and utility work should likewise be planned and conducted with the safety and accessibility of all motorists, bicyclists, pedestrians (including those with disabilities), and workers considered at all times, and early coordination with the railroad or light rail transit agency should occur if the TTC zone includes a grade crossing. - General plans or guidelines should be developed to provide safety for motorists, bicyclists, pedestrians, workers, and enforcement/emergency officials; the basic safety principles governing permanent roadways should also govern TTC zone design, with the goal of routing road users through TTC zones using geometrics, roadside features, and devices as comparable as possible to normal highway conditions; a TTC plan appropriate to the project's complexity should be prepared and understood before the site is occupied, with changes approved by a knowledgeable official; and road user movement should be inhibited as little as practical, avoiding frequent and abrupt geometric changes. - Temporary traffic control operations should minimize inconvenience, delay, and crash potential to affected traffic, and prior notice should be given to affected agencies, emergency services, businesses, railroad companies or transit agencies, and road users before free movement is infringed upon or blocked. Support (informational context): - TTC planning provides for continuity of motor vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian traffic movement (including accessible passage), transit operations, and access (and accessibility) to property and utilities when the normal function of a roadway is suspended. - At grade crossings, TTC planning similarly provides for continuity of operations when the normal roadway function is suspended, and is also needed when traffic is detoured over an existing grade crossing. - The MUTCD's overall purpose is to establish uniform national criteria for traffic control devices that meet the needs and expectancy of road users on all facilities open to public travel. Citations: - Section 6A.02 Guidance §1 (p.766) - Section 6A.02 Guidance §2 (p.768) - Section 8A.13 Guidance §7 (p.992) - Section 6A.01 Support §3 (p.765) - Section 8A.13 Support §1 (p.992) - Section 1A.01 Support §1 (p.1)
gold_answer: Road-user and worker safety and accessibility must be treated as integral, high-priority considerations from planning through design and construction, including motorists, bicyclists, pedestrians with disabilities, workers, and coordination with rail transit where applicable.
